title: [Decision] Should Studio show changes staged or published from outside the browser tab (MCP, REST, another tab) without a manual reload — and by polling or by a server push?
body:
eval#1 · os-bob · session_012dn2AcTB69pEwZ9ugr1g1w

Filing gate: ② a decision only the maintainer can make.

## 维护者速读

- 现象:通过 MCP 修改元数据(落成草稿)后,已经打开的 Studio 页面上「变更」角标和草稿标记都不变,看起来像"没改成";必须手动刷新浏览器才能看到。反过来,在 Studio 发布后回到 MCP 也无从得知。只有打开「变更」抽屉那一刻会重读列表。
- 要你裁:Studio 是否要对"本标签页之外"的元数据变更自动刷新,以及走哪种形状(前端轮询/聚焦重取,还是服务端推送)。
- 推荐:B → C 分期 — 先在 `usePendingDrafts` 加"窗口重新获得焦点时重取 + 页面可见时低频轮询",一个 PR 解决今天的困惑;再把草稿变更接入已有的 realtime 通道,作为终态。

## One-sentence problem

When an agent changes the app over MCP, the Studio page the user already has open keeps showing the old state — no pending-change badge, no draft marks — until the user thinks to reload the browser, so a change that worked looks like a change that failed.

## Evidence (reach)

Session on the `os-dev-test` environment (framework `c110853e`): metadata drafts staged by MCP authoring tools (`apply_edit`, `update_metadata`, `create_seed`) did not appear in an open Studio tab's Changes badge until a manual browser reload; the user reported it as "Studio 页面上看不到是否已变更".

Code reading (all re-checkable):
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/preview/usePendingDrafts.ts` — the single source of the pending-drafts count (`GET /api/v1/meta/_drafts`). It refetches on mount, scope change and the in-tab `subscribeMetadataRefresh` pulse (:248) only; no polling, no focus/visibility refetch. Re-check: `grep -n "setInterval\|visibilitychange\|subscribeMetadataRefresh" ui/packages/app-shell/src/preview/usePendingDrafts.ts`.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/assistant/assistantBus.ts:156-169` — the refresh bus is an in-memory per-tab listener set; it is pulsed by Studio's own saves/publishes and by the in-console AI chat (`console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx` ~:2425), which is why Studio refreshes for its own copilot but never for an external MCP client.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/preview/DraftChangesPanel.tsx` ~:1629 — the Changes sheet re-reads its list each time it opens; the badge and per-item draft marks do not.
- Server: a draft save emits `emitMetadataMutation({ state: 'draft' })` in-process only; the cluster fan-out returns early for drafts (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-mutation-fan-out.ts:115`, `protocol-class-head.ts:375`), and `MetadataManager.publishRealtimeMetadataEvent` fires only from `register()`/delete, never for drafts. Re-check: `grep -n "state === 'draft') return" packages/metadata-protocol/src/*.ts`.
- The only browser push for metadata is the dev-only HMR SSE (`GET /api/v1/dev/metadata-events`, `NODE_ENV=development`; client `ui/apps/console/src/components/MetadataHmrReloader.tsx`, `import.meta.env.DEV`, full `location.reload()`).
- The QA checklist already records the gap as expected: `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/studio-authoring.json` item `studio-authoring.draft-publish-lifecycle` — "A publish made outside Studio (the REST publish …) shows in Studio only after a reload". Re-check: `grep -n "only after a reload" docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/studio-authoring.json`.

## Governing text

- `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` line 7 — "Two kinds of user: today, business staff through the UI …; tomorrow, agents through MCP. Every step of the road must hold for both kinds of user." An agent's change that the UI user cannot see breaks the hand-off between the two.
- `docs/adr/0008-metadata-repository-and-change-log.md` (~:140-170) — describes a change log with `seq` and `watch()/subscribe(since=seq)` with an SSE/WS broadcast; only the dev HMR stream was built.
- `docs/adr/0037-live-canvas-draft-preview.md` Phase 2 (~:68-73) — live refresh via `assistantBus` for the in-console chat only; external clients are out of its scope.
- Protocol change? No spec change for A/B; C adds draft events to the realtime channel (a server contract), which needs an ADR-0008 amendment.

## Options

| Option | What it does | What the customer sees | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Keep today's behaviour; document "reload to see changes made outside Studio" | Agent says "改好了", Studio shows nothing until reload | none (doc line) |
| B | Client-side: `usePendingDrafts` (and the package metadata refresh) also refetch on window focus / `visibilitychange`, plus a low-frequency poll (e.g. 15–30 s) while the tab is visible | Switching back to the Studio tab shows the agent's changes within a moment; an idle visible tab catches up within the poll interval | ui seat · 1 PR · no measured precedent; small (one hook + its consumers' pulse) |
| C | Server push: forward draft (and publish) metadata mutations to the existing `service-realtime` channel (`metadata.<type>.drafted/published`), and have the console subscribe (`RealtimeAPI.subscribeMetadata` exists in the client SDK, unused) and pulse `emitMetadataRefresh` | Changes appear live, in every open tab, including from MCP/REST/other users | server + ui seats · 2–3 PRs · ADR-0008 amendment · no measured precedent |

Business reading: A = "refresh the page" stays a user chore; B = the page catches up when you look at it; C = the page is live, like a shared document.

## Recommendation

C as the end state, delivered B first. Two years out Studio and an agent edit the same app concurrently, and every mainstream collaborative builder shows other writers' changes live (Figma, Notion, Retool multiplayer; Salesforce setup at least warns on stale metadata). ADR-0008 already describes the change-log subscription this needs; only the dev stream exists. B is the timing step, not a different letter: it fixes today's confusion in one PR and stays useful as the fallback when a push connection drops. Not A: it leaves the agent/UI hand-off broken, which is exactly the North Star's "both kinds of user" road.
Confidence gap: the realtime service's availability and fan-out cost per tenant for draft-level events are unmeasured; C should be scoped to the package the tab is showing.
Self-check: only ① picks C (B as its first phase); ②③④ do not flip it — ② and ④ only set the B-first timing.

## After the ruling

Phase 1 (B): `usePendingDrafts` refetches on focus/visibility and polls while visible; Studio's item draft marks and the package metadata resolver listen to the same pulse; drop the "only after a reload" clause from `studio-authoring.draft-publish-lifecycle`. e2e: stage a draft via REST/MCP, switch back to an open Studio tab, the badge updates without reload.
Phase 2 (C): draft/publish mutations published on `service-realtime`; the console subscribes once per tab and pulses `emitMetadataRefresh`; ADR-0008 amended.

os-decision-facets
① 项目长远合理性: C 落地 ADR-0008 已描述的变更订阅,让 UI 与 agent 共编同一应用时状态一致;B 是其分期第一步与断线兜底,A 让两类用户之间的交接长期断开。
② 实际业务拉动: 今天每个用 MCP 搭应用、同时开着 Studio 的用户都会撞上(本次会话实测),且 QA 清单已把"外部发布需刷新"记成预期行为。
③ 防 AI 犯错: 看不到变更时,用户会以为 AI 没改成而让它重做,导致重复/冲突修改;B/C 让结果可见,错误更容易被及时发现。
④ 创业阶段不扩散: B 只改一个 hook、无新契约;C 新增 realtime 事件需维护,故按 B → C 分期。
Prior rulings read: "Studio drafts reload / Studio changes refresh" → 12 hits (#32440, #25943, #29672 — none rule on cross-tab/external refresh); ADR-0008, ADR-0037; thread: none

Reader who acts: the `ui/` app-shell seat (phase 1) and the metadata/realtime server seat (phase 2), after the ruling.
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue Studio changes refresh` → 6 hits, `Studio drafts reload` → 6 hits, none on external-change refresh.
